logline: In the aftermath of a mass disappearance that claimed 2% of the world's population, the survivors of a small New York town fracture under grief, cult religion, and the impossibility of moving on.

renewal.note: Three-season run concluded June 4, 2017. Damon Lindelof and Tom Perrotta designed the final season as a series conclusion; no continuation has been announced.

bollymeter.basis: 82% on RT from 182 critics; critics praised its formal ambition and somber courage but noted its relentless dourness as a legitimate barrier, reflected in a Metacritic of 65.

pull_quotes.text: Its dour tone and self-seriousness may make for somber viewing, but The Leftovers is artfully crafted and thought-provoking.

seasons.review_body: The first season of The Leftovers, premiering June 2014, adapted Tom Perrotta's novel directly - the small town of Mapleton, New York, three years after the Sudden Departure. Critics gave it 82% from 182 reviews, with the consensus acknowledging its artisanal quality while flagging unrelieved bleakness as a real viewing cost. Metacritic placed it at 65, reflecting a meaningful minority who found the grief-soaked texture exhausting rather than immersive. Justin Theroux anchored the season as police chief Kevin Garvey, and the Guilty Remnant cult provided one of American television's most unsettling factions. It is a difficult, formally serious season - rewarding but not easy.

episode_reviews.title: Two Boats and a Helicopter
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A bottle episode focused entirely on the Reverend Matt Jamison (Christopher Eccleston), attempting to save his church from foreclosure in a single day. Critics singled it out as the season's best hour - a parable about faith, luck, and the cruelty of a post-departure world that functions as a complete short film.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The coin landing that decides whether years of faith were rewarded or pointless - a moment that divides audiences on whether to call it miracle or chance.

bollymeter.basis: 94% on RT from 164 critics; a second season that relocated to Texas, introduced Carrie Coon, and transformed an already unusual show into one of television's great reinventions.

pull_quotes.text: The Leftovers continues to be unpredictable and provocative in season two, though its inexplicable circumstances will still frustrate many viewers.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 relocated to Jarden, Texas - a town where no one disappeared during the Sudden Departure - and the move unlocked something extraordinary. Critics jumped from 82% to 94% from 164 reviews, and audience enthusiasm on IMDb reached 9.3, one of the highest season ratings for any prestige drama. Carrie Coon's Nora Durst became the show's emotional center, and Lindelof committed to stranger, more formally experimental storytelling - including an episode narrated entirely from the perspective of a National Geographic-style wildlife documentary. The Leftovers stopped being merely serious and started becoming genuinely radical.
seasons.season_over_season: A near-total reinvention - new location, new family at the center, and a formal ambition that left Season 1's adaptation roots entirely behind.

episode_reviews.title: International Assassin
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Kevin Garvey wakes in a surreal, hotel-based alternate reality and must complete a mission he does not understand in order to return. The episode abandons conventional television grammar almost entirely and operates as something closer to a Kafka-inflected fever dream. It is the hour most cited when critics argue the show belongs among the all-time greats.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The hotel corridor sequences where the rules keep shifting - an experience of television as pure, bewildering cinema that critics struggled to find comparisons for.

bollymeter.basis: 99% on RT from 189 critics with a Metacritic of 98 - numbers that place it among the most acclaimed final seasons of any drama series in television history.

pull_quotes.text: With reliably ambitious storytelling and outstanding performances, Season 3 of The Leftovers approaches its conclusion as thoughtfully, purposefully, and confidently as it began.

seasons.review_body: The final eight episodes aired April-June 2017 and landed a 99% on Rotten Tomatoes from 189 critics - a Metacritic of 98 puts it in the company of the most universally acclaimed last seasons in television history. IndieWire titled its review 'A Perfectly Timed Masterpiece.' The season relocated the action to Australia and resolved - or deliberately refused to resolve - the show's central mystery with a finale that critics overwhelmingly called earned, devastating, and formally perfect. Carrie Coon's final episode performance drew specific comparisons to the best screen acting of the decade. Screen Rant noted the show deserves even more than its already rare scores suggest.
seasons.season_over_season: The series finishes stronger than almost any prestige drama attempted; the audience score rose to 91% Popcornmeter, erasing the hesitance that marked Season 1 reception.

episode_reviews.title: The Book of Nora
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series finale centers on Nora Durst and the question of whether the truth she claims to carry matters more than the life she could still have. Lindelof and Perrotta decline to answer every question they posed, and critics were near-unanimous that this refusal was the correct artistic choice. Carrie Coon's final scene is the one people mean when they say television can be literature.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Nora's account of where she went - offered quietly, without spectacle - and Kevin's choice of whether to believe her.

critic_note.text: An obituary of one of the greatest shows in the history of TV.
